Desktop-only bundled plugins and the upstream import pin live here. Harness source is the monorepo root and is not duplicated under this directory.

The desktop installer bundles each vendored tree offline through electron-builder `extraResources`, which copies the directory whole — so whatever a plugin needs at runtime has to be on disk before the pack, not only in a registry. Two kinds of subtree satisfy that, and they are handled differently.

A complete plugin's compiled half is tracked. `rlhmarket/lib` is committed build output with no source in this tree, so [`../.gitignore`](../.gitignore) un-ignores it by name against the repository-wide `lib/` ignore. `rlhbot/lib` is absent and cannot be regenerated or fetched; `ensureRlhbotPlugin` validates `main` and every local `exports` entry before touching the profile, removes any older managed copy when validation fails, and leaves rlhbot unmounted until a complete package is restored.

Every vendored plugin has a version-3 npm lock matching its manifest, including declared Host peers. Every production dependency needs a fixed HTTPS resolution and integrity; missing or inconsistent locks fail before an existing install is removed. `rlhmarket` locks `js-yaml` 4.3.1, `argparse` 2.0.1, and `undici` 7.29.0. Its compiled settings entry also declares the Host's `@relay-harness/schemastery` peer. The `rlhbot` lock has no production packages because its dependencies are Host peers; its absent `lib` still makes it unmountable, never installable merely because a lock exists.

A plugin's dependencies are installed, not tracked. Development `vendor:sync` reuses only matching package versions with a valid lock. Release `after-pack` always performs a fresh `npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --legacy-peer-deps --workspaces=false --no-fund --no-audit` in the packaged plugin, then verifies runtime entry files. Host peers come from the existing Harness, not copied SDK/Cordis installations. No release path falls back to an unlocked `npm install`. Air-gapped builders need the locked tarballs already cached; an unavailable tarball fails the pack rather than silently changing its dependencies.

[`plugins.json`](plugins.json) records each vendored plugin's upstream source, the version pinned, and any subtree the drop does not carry, with the reason. [`vendor-plugins.test.js`](vendor-plugins.test.js) checks every entry point a plugin's `package.json` declares against that record, fails when a subtree listed as absent turns up — so a restored subtree cannot stay recorded as missing, and the suites that skip on it cannot stay skipped — and fails when an install is committed or drifts from its lockfile. That inventory permits an incomplete archival drop to remain in the repository; installer admission is stricter and never treats a recorded absence as a loadable package.

A top-level directory is a vendored plugin only when it contains `package.json`. Ignored `lib/`-only residue left by an older checkout or a pre-rebrand build is not packaged and must not be added to `plugins.json`; remove that local residue instead.
